meta.title: LTV should be about 3× CAC
meta.summary: SAMPLE CAC $40, $20/mo, 3 months → LTV $60 → 1.5×, weak vs 3×.

success.message:
Session complete. LTV ≈ price × months; smell LTV/CAC around 3×.

SAMPLE: $60/$40=1.5× weak; $120/$40=3×.

start.message:
SAMPLE: CAC $40, price $20/mo, they stay 3 months.

LTV first?

choices.label: Assume 12 months because SaaS is annual

wrong_start_cac_only.message:
CAC needs LTV. $40 might be cheap or fatal depending on life.

Return to LTV.

wrong_start_year.message:
The SAMPLE said 3 months. Do not upgrade the life.

Return to LTV.

ratio.message:
LTV $60 / CAC $40.

Ratio vs the 3× rule?

choices.label: 40/60 ≈ 0.67×, so CAC is 67% of LTV and that is the 3×

wrong_ratio_three.message:
60/40=1.5. 3× would need $120 LTV.

Revisit the ratio.

wrong_ratio_invert.message:
The taught ratio is LTV/CAC, target ~3.

Revisit the ratio.

wrong_check_still_thin.message:
CAC did not change; LTV did. 120/40=3.

Try the check again.

wrong_check_twelve.message:
Do not shove price into the ratio twice. LTV already used it.

Try the check again.
